{{Short description|Chinese-American physicist}}
'''Eugene Chen Loh''' (1 October 1934 – May 19, 2006)<ref>Legacy (25-27 MAY 2006).  Eugene Chen Loh, Obituary.  Legacy Remembers.  Link still valid 22 APR 2023: [https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/eugene-loh-obituary?id=29005885]</ref> was a Chinese American physicist, having been Distinguished Professor Emeritus at [[University of Utah]] and was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>Univ. of Utah (16 NOV 2022).  Distinguished Professors List (updated). Academic Affairs, University of Utah. Public reference URL still valid 25 APR 2023: [https://academic-affairs.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/18/2022/11/Distinguished-Professors-List-2022.pdf]</ref>

==Biography==
Loh spent his childhood in [[Suzhou, Jiangsu|Suzhou, China]] and emigrated to Virginia with his family at 14. He received his BS from [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute]] and his PhD from [[MIT]]. He took his first faculty job at [[Cornell University]] before moving to the [[University of Utah]] in 1975. He led the team to build the [[High Resolution Fly's Eye Cosmic Ray Detector]] at the US Army's [[Dugway Proving Ground]], which in 1991 recorded the most energetic [[cosmic ray]] ever detected, known as the "[[Oh-My-God particle]]".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lavine|first1=Greg|title=Physicist tracked cosmic rays|url=http://archive.sltrib.com/story.php?ref=/search/ci_3862259|accessdate=22 May 2017|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|agency=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=25 May 2006}}</ref> He received the [[Utah Governor's Medal for Science and Technology]] in 1987. In 1998, Dr. Loh became rotating Program Director of Astrophysics at the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://archive.unews.utah.edu/news_releases/u-cosmic-ray-pioneer-gene-loh-dies-at-72/ |title=U Cosmic Ray Pioneer Gene Loh Dies at 72 |date=May 24, 2006 |publisher=utah.edu |accessdate=March 5, 2017}}</ref> In 1982, as chairman, Department of Physics, University of Utah, Prof. Loh, along with former chairman, Prof. Peter Godbe Gibbs, and Physicist Prof. William D. Ohlsen, supervised and approved the M.S. Physics thesis, "Flexible Response Modes of Missile Experimental: Multiple Aim Points System and Deception Dense Pack", by Robert Donald Green, then also a doctoral candidate at University of Pennsylvania.<ref>Green, Robert Donald (1982). Flexible Response Modes of Missile Experimental: Multiple Aim Points System and Deception Dense Pack. Thesis for the Master of Science degree in Physics, The University of Utah.</ref> The University of Utah's ''U Alumni'' interviewed allied defense Physicist Dr Green in 2024.<ref>Dr R Don Green, Physics BS’77 MS’82 Public Administration MPA’81, PhD, in Utah Alumni Stories (11/15/2024). U Alumni, University of Utah: https://ulink.utah.edu/s/1077/23/1col.aspx?sid=1077&gid=1&pgid=5491&cid=16432&ecid=16432&crid=0&calpgid=2187&calcid=15283</ref>
